item.title: Decoding the North American bison's genome to better inform conservation efforts
item.description: [Science & Research] Keyword: genomics — A new study by ancient DNA researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, used paleogenomics to create a genetic roadmap to help guide the restoration of another iconic species once on the brink of extinction: the North American bison.

item.title: Poll suggests US adults are facing increased strain from extreme heat
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — More than half of Americans told the AP-NORC poll that climate change is happening, a slight decline from last year.

item.title: One-third of agricultural land accounts for two-thirds of global impact, study reveals
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Agriculture covers more than 40% of Earth's habitable land and plays a central role in both climate change and biodiversity loss. Yet the impact of agriculture is far from evenly distributed across space.

item.title: "Fire Climate": Hot, Dry, Windy Days Are Becoming Common, Making Wildfires Harder to Control
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — The Pacific Northwest is facing its worst fire season in more than 30 years. Scientists say drought, extreme heat and climate change are making wildfire seasons longer, more frequent and more destructive across the western United States. “The homes, the communities, they’re just not simply prepared for fire,” says Paul Hessburg, former senior research ecologist at the U.S. Forest Service and professor of fire and landscape ecology at the University of Washington.
